newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill 90 guerrillas - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill 90 guerrillas - paper.

text.p: Algerian troops, besieging hundreds of hardline Armed Islamic Group (GIA) guerrillas gathered in congress, have so far killed more than 90 rebels in a continuing huge operation, an Algerian newspaper said on Monday.
GIA chief Antar Zouabri, 27, might be among the trapped men in a rugged area near Attatba in Blida province, about 50 km (about 30 miles) south of Algiers, L'Authentique newspaper said.
Hundreds of GIA rebels had gone to the group base there from Algiers and other regions to attend a congress to plot ways to step up their campaign against the government, it said.
The authorities blame the GIA for the massacres of hundreds of villagers in remote areas, for bombings in cities and killing leading journalists and intellectuals.

"Their (the rebels) goal has been very clear: exchanging information and coordinating their criminal activities with the aim of deploying with maximum efficiency in the field," said L'authentique outlining the apparent aim of the congress.
The huge military swoop began a week ago with a limited operation against a small rebel gang before the security forces stumbled onto what the newspaper described as a GIA base.
Crack troops threw a seamless cordon around the base while bomb disposal experts cleared the way for the soldiers' advance, it said.
"The intricacy of the situation needed the intervention of elite army troops and bomb disposal experts who have defused dozens of bombs," L'Authentique said.
Army commandos, pursuing a "search and destroy" strategy, have up to now killed more than 90 rebels and forced a "great number" of others to surrender, the newspaper said.
The security forces recovered more than 100 arms, including Kalashnikov assault rifles and automatic pistols, the paper said.
"Indisputably, the security forces scored another victory in their tireless work to wipe out armed groups," the paper added.
Another newspaper, El Watan, at the weekend gave a similar version of the operation saying the security forces had killed more than 60 rebels.
Le Matin newspaper in a feature on Monday described the horror of Algeria's violence, saying one hospital in Algiers had treated about 600 casualties in the first seven months of this year.
The newspaper said among the dead the hospital had received were 23 people who had their throats cut and 28 killed in bomb blasts.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
